finding.claim: Unauthenticated cross-customer invoice read: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns the full invoice (including customer) for any ID with no auth or ownership check.
finding.source: inv_id path segment from an unauthenticated remote client

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator
Lookup by attacker-supplied ID with no caller identity
Sibling /my/invoice route enforces ownership; this route does not

finding.guards_checked: No auth decorator on route; no ownership check in handler; no before_request/auth middleware in this file; no bind address or proxy config in this file (ingress depends on deployment). Caveat: auth hook outside this file would void the finding; INVOICES is an empty in-file dict so ID enumerability is unknown. Validation tier 0 (single curl request).

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 has no auth decorator, and invoices.py:9-10 looks up INVOICES.get(inv_id) and returns jsonify(inv) with no ownership check. The only other code in the directory is the .claude/skills/*.md documentation, which contains no middleware or before_request hook. The sibling route at invoices.py:16-17 does enforce ownership, so the contrast the claim relies on is real.
verdict.reason: The route at invoices.py:7 returns any invoice by ID at invoices.py:9-10 with no check of caller identity, and the only in-repo guard (the ownership check at invoices.py:16-17) is on the sibling /my/invoice route, so an anonymous attacker can read any invoice. The one caveat is that invoices.py:16 reads g.user, which is never set in this file, so an external before_request auth hook elsewhere in the deployed app could cover this route and void the finding; that code is not in the repo, so I can't rule it out.

finding.claim: /my/* routes rely on an undefined g.user with no explicit auth guard; unauthenticated requests error (500) rather than returning 401. Hardening gap, not a bypass.
finding.source: Unauthenticated request in which g.user is never set

trace.note: Ownership comparison dereferences g.user; raises if unset

finding.guards_checked: Ownership comparison blocks cross-customer reads; handler returns 404 for both missing and not-owned invoices (no existence oracle). No bypass found. Debug-mode traceback exposure depends on settings not visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth decorator or before_request hook exists in invoices.py or elsewhere in the directory, and nothing assigns g.user. The only check is the ownership comparison at invoices.py:16, which dereferences g.user and so fails for anonymous requests rather than blocking them.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: /my/invoice/<inv_id> (invoices.py:13-16) and /my/invoices (invoices.py:21-23) dereference g.user with no guard, and an anonymous request reaches that line with g.user unset, so it fails with an error instead of returning 401. This is a hardening gap with no authorization bypass, so the severity should stay low, and the claim is accurate as written.
